'''Joan Bagaria Pigrau''' (born August 17, 1958) is a Catalan mathematician, logician and [[set theory|set theorist]] at [[Catalan Institution for Research and Advanced Studies|ICREA]] and [[University of Barcelona]]. He has made many contributions concerning [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]], [[large cardinals]], infinite combinatorics and their applications to other areas of mathematics.

== Biography ==

=== Early life (1958 – 1992) ===
Bagaria was born in 1958 in [[Manlleu]], Catalonia, Spain.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Bagaria |first=Joan |date=2023 |title=CURRICULUM VITAE |url=https://www.icrea.cat/security/files/researchers/files-maintenance/joanbagariacompletecv2023.pdf |access-date=18 July 2024 |website=www.icrea.cat}}</ref> He earned a B.A. in philosophy from the [[University of Barcelona]] in 1981, and an M.A. in philosophy there in 1984.<ref name=":0" /> He earned his PhD in Logic & the Methodology of Science at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1991 under the supervision of Haim Judah and [[W. Hugh Woodin]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{MathGenealogy|id=24631}}</ref> He also held various other positions at UC Berkeley between January 1986 and May 1992, including as a reader, a graduate student instructor, a junior specialist, and a summer session instructor.<ref name=":0" />

=== Career (1992 – present) ===
In June 1992, Bagaria returned to Catalonia as an invited researcher at the [[Centre de Recerca Matemàtica]], where he remained until that September.<ref name=":0" /> From October 1992 to September 1995, he was an interim research professor at the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]].<ref name=":0" /> He was an invited professor at [[Pompeu Fabra University]] from October 1995 to September 1996.<ref name=":0" /> Then he got an interim associate professor position at University of Barcelona, which he held until October 2001.<ref name=":0" />

Since 2001, he has been ICREA Research Professor at [[University of Barcelona]].<ref>[[ORCID]] Page [https://orcid.org/0000-0002-4686-8222]</ref> He served as the first president of the European Set Theory Society (2007–11).

His research work is widely cited,<ref>Data in [[Scopus]]: [https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=6603007630]</ref> and he has given talks to the general public.<ref>[[Turing]]'s Legacy in Mathematical Logic and Foundation of Mathematics [http://www.fundacionareces.tv/watch/alaturing?as=50a666b7c31997e15f010000] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180503042724/http://www.fundacionareces.tv/watch/alaturing?as=50a666b7c31997e15f010000|date=May 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>[http://srvcnpbs.xtec.cat/creamat/joomla/index.php/matematiques-en-accio/1301-matematiques-en-accio-joan-bagaria-recerca-en-fonaments-matematics- Matemàtiques en acció]</ref> He has had nine PhD students.<ref name=":1" />

=== Personal life ===
He is also an active [[Catalan independence movement|Catalan independentist]].<ref>[[VilaWeb]]'s coverage [https://www.vilaweb.cat/noticies/el-suport-de-la-comunitat-cientifica-a-la-independencia-un-debat-intens/]</ref>
